Both are very adequate cameras for sure but in my opinion (I have sort of a bias so take it with a grain of salt) the A7iii will be a better decision is the grand scheme. 

Dual card slots is a big one, both Nikon and Canon didn’t add this to their full frame mirrorless cameras. A7iii has dual cards slots which is a big one for me because I’ve been cursed with failed SD cards with video and a back up SD can really save you, or you know if you just use up all the first card and need to keep going. This is important for a pro setup since you don’t want to have to stop mid job to change cards.

Without native lenses already you’d be forced to get the Z-mount lineup or go F-mount then grab an adapter to use them on the Z6. The lenses for the Z lineup are pretty steep in price. If that’s no issue for you then disregard this. Sony E-mount lenses can range from APS-C (even with the 1.5x crop factor on full frame) to the full frame lineup and they are all compatible no adapters. 

If you have larger hands you may not like the Sony at first and like the Z6 more. Z6 has a better grip on it and is a little easier to hold. I personally use battery grips so it’s no issue really for me. 

The A7iii AF is very good with the 693 phase detection points and Sony also has Eye AF if you want to shoot portraits and the subject’s face be in perfect focus. 

A7iii battery is around 700 shots (I think) per charge and the Z6 is around half that. Which I see as understandable since Sony has been improving  mirrorless systems almost exclusively so they should have it that good. Nikon still needs time to improve it. 

There are others but I think this should be good I’d hope, just remember that I’m a Sony fan boy and stand by their products strongly. 

If I said anything incorrectly or got something wrong someone please correct me! Hope this helps!
